page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem provides 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for in-memory footprints. In addition to general instance capacity, the r5dn.2xlarge bundles 300 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local instance storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps without integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results reflect balanced execution for multi-threaded and memory-intensive tasks, accompanied by lower single-threaded throughput. The instance recorded average tier outcomes in multi-core benchmarks, including a PassMark CPU score of 7626.07, a Geekbench multi-core score of 4404.0, and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 6870.73. Conversely, single-core metrics sit within the lower 25 percent bracket across stress-ng, Geekbench, and gzip compression. Memory performance aligns with middle-tier standards, registering 51.32 GB/s large-block read bandwidth, 40.38 GB/s write bandwidth, and delivering 6.38 million operations per second in Redis SET operations alongside average database operation scores.

The qualitative trade-off of this hardware configuration centers on memory and fast local storage availability versus compute intensity. While the high memory-to-core ratio and local NVMe storage deliver effective resource density for data operations, compute-heavy tasks like LLM inference evaluate poorly on this processor. The r5dn.2xlarge is functionally well positioned for in-memory caching layers, relational databases requiring fast scratch storage, ETL pipelines, and data processing tasks requiring substantial RAM buffers.
description: Amazon Web Services r5dn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server featuring an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores. It provides 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, paired with 300 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 8 Gbps baseline network throughput on the Nitro hypervisor. Benchmark evaluations show middle-tier execution across multi-core tests, PassMark memory performance, and Redis SET operations, which achieve 6.38 million operations per second, counterbalanced by modest single-threaded compute results and limited machine learning inference capabilities. The high memory density and fast local ephemeral storage make the r5dn.2xlarge a solid choice for caching servers, in-memory databases, and intermediate data processing workloads.
